tests.title: Active route displays only active todos
tests.summary: With a known active todo and a known completed todo, navigate to #/active and prove that only the active item belongs to the displayed view.

steps.heading: Step 1
steps.text: Open {{start_url}} in the browser and, on the TodoMVC todo page, establish an active todo titled {{active_todo_title}} and a completed todo titled {{completed_todo_title}} using the new-todo input and each todo's completion checkbox.

steps.heading: Step 2
steps.text: On the TodoMVC page's footer filter links, navigate to Active (#/active), then assert the Active filter link has the `selected` class.

steps.heading: Step 3
steps.text: On the Active view's todo list, inspect the displayed todo titles and completion states, then assert every displayed todo is active, {{active_todo_title}} is present, and {{completed_todo_title}} is absent.

steps.heading: Step 1

steps.heading: Step 2

The React 19 + TypeScript port is in `~/contri/todomvc-react-port`, and both `npm install` and `npm run build` succeed. The build writes a static site to `dist/` with Vite's `base` set to `'./'`. I haven't opened the built site in a browser, so the behaviour comparison below comes from reading the legacy code, not from running both side by side.

- **Look:** I copied the legacy `base.css` and `index.css` into `src/` unchanged. I left out `app.css`, because it only hid `#main` and `#footer` until jQuery showed them. React now renders those two sections only when they should appear.
- **Behaviour I reproduced from `app.js`:**
  - Todos are created on Enter, using keyup as the legacy app does.
  - Double-click edits a todo, Enter or blur saves it, and Escape cancels.
  - Saving an empty title deletes the todo.
  - Toggle-all, "Clear completed", and the "item"/"items" wording in the count all work as before.
  - The filter follows `#/all`, `#/active` and `#/completed`.
  - "Clear completed" resets the filter to All.
  - The new-todo input regains focus after every change.
- **No persistence:** the legacy `util.store` is a stub that always returns `[]`, so todos are lost on reload. I kept that rather than add storage.
- **Dropped:** I did not carry over `base.js`, the sidebar loader the legacy page included.

There is one small difference. Todo ids now come from `crypto.randomUUID()` instead of the hand-rolled UUID function, which users won't see.
